title: A free boundary problem for the mean-field limit of diffusing particles with nonlinear boundary reactivity
summary: Consider a finite system of diffusing particles coupled through a reactive boundary. Each particle is reflected, but may react with the boundary according to a killing mechanism which depends on the current reactivity of the boundary and the particle's local time along it. With every such reaction, the boundary moves and its reactivity adjusts. We show that this system admits a unique mean-field limit, described by a free boundary problem with nonlinear and nonlocal reactivity.
